acceptance.criterion: Fix the parallel-load flake first, and note it is worse than first recorded: 25 cases across 5 projects (not 8, not 4), false-passes AND false-fails, guest-list-scroll.spec.ts:55 the observed false-fail moving between Pixel 7 and Desktop Chrome across two full-suite runs. Find the actual race, fix the cause not the symptom, and prove both directions closed.
acceptance.evidence: Suite confirmed 25 cases / 5 projects (5 tests x 4 spec files x 5 projects) via `npx playwright test e2e/layout --list` -> 'Total: 25 tests in 4 files'. Root cause reproduced: added a 600ms delay to e2e/support/api-mocks.ts's json() helper (reverted immediately after each experiment; final `diff` against the pre-session copy is empty) and ran `npx playwright test e2e/layout` — reproduced 'Error: no scrollable ancestor found above .table-row' on Pixel 7 (Chrome Android), Desktop Chrome, and iPhone 14, on both guest-list-scroll.spec.ts:55 and pinned-regions.spec.ts, on the first attempt. Mechanism: guest-manager.html's `initialLoading()` branch renders its own 8-row skeleton under `.table-row` (identical class name to the real, data-backed rows) inside a `.table-container` that carries no `role` attribute (`aria-hidden="true"` instead) — only the real table carries `role="table"`. Under worker contention the mocked fetch can resolve slower than the skeleton's first paint, so a bare `page.locator('.table-row').first().toBeVisible()` or `document.querySelector('.table-row')` can resolve against the 8-row skeleton; on a viewport tall/wide enough that 8 short rows do not overflow the scroll region (Desktop Chrome and Pixel 7's viewports, occasionally iPhone 14's), the ancestor-walk in guest-list-scroll.spec.ts:66/pinned-regions.spec.ts:39 finds nothing scrollable and throws exactly the observed error — explaining both 'no scrollable ancestor' and 'the moving project is the tell' (which project fails is whichever happened to be slowest that run and has a tall/wide-enough viewport, not a CSS regression pinned to one engine). guest-list-scroll.spec.ts:23 and the pageSize test never showed this because it gates on `toHaveCount(20)`, which the 8-row skeleton can never satisfy. Fix: scoped every `.table-row` query in the four layout specs to `.table-container[role="table"] .table-row` (e2e/layout/pinned-regions.spec.ts, e2e/layout/guest-list-scroll.spec.ts, e2e/layout/clip-flex-item.spec.ts) — this is what makes Playwright's own auto-wait retry past the skeleton instead of resolving against it; no config, retry count, or waitForTimeout added. playwright.config.ts left unmodified (confirmed via `git diff --stat playwright.config.ts` — no output). False-fail direction closed: 5 consecutive clean `npx playwright test e2e/layout` runs, 25/25 passed each (run outputs captured in this session's transcript, e.g. '25 passed (31.8s)', '25 passed (24.9s)', '25 passed (21.1s)', '25 passed (20.9s)', '25 passed (19.6s)'), plus 5 more runs under the same 600ms artificial delay that reliably reproduced the failure before the fix, all 25/25 ('25 passed (34.0s)', '25 passed (35.3s)', '25 passed (34.7s)', plus two more, run twice before and after the delay round-trip). False-pass direction closed: removed `min-height: 0` from `main` in src/app/layouts/private-layout/private-layout.scss (the exact declaration clip-flex-item.spec.ts's own header comment documents as the historical defect) and re-ran `npx playwright test e2e/layout` under the full parallel suite — 20 of 25 cases failed (every case touching clip-flex-item.spec.ts, guest-list-scroll.spec.ts, and pinned-regions.spec.ts, across all 5 projects; footer-truncation.spec.ts's 5 cases correctly kept passing, since that declaration is unrelated to what it asserts), then reverted the break (`git diff src/app/layouts/private-layout/private-layout.scss` — no output, confirmed clean).

risks.risk: The skeleton/real-content class-name collision that caused this flake (`.table-row` shared between guest-manager's initialLoading() skeleton and its real table) is a pattern, not a one-off — config-manager, milestones, seating-plan and people may render their own loading skeletons with the same class names as their real content. Any T343/T350 spec that locates content by a bare class name without checking whether that screen has a skeleton state risks the identical race.
